extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and their representatives entering the European phase (EPO) from a PCT international application (including professional representatives and patent attorneys)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and procedural requirements, time limits, fees, language and representation rules for entering the European (EPO) national phase from a PCT international application. Covers forms, translations, fees, searches, examination, and consequences of non‑compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits applicable for entry into the national phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PCT Article 22(3): 31 months from the priority date. Under PCT Article 39(1)(b): 31 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 31 months is the principal time limit referred to throughout the chapter for paying fees, filing translations and other acts for entry into the European phase; some specific fees or acts may have alternative later time limits (e.g. six months after publication of the international search report) — the applicable later deadline applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of international application (languages required)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Euro‑PCT application was not published in an EPO official language, the applicant must submit a translation into one of the EPO official languages: English, French or German.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translation must be submitted within the 31‑month time limit (see EP.03). The language of proceedings will be the published language or the language of the translation submitted; the language of proceedings cannot be changed subsequently (EP.02). Errors in the translation can be corrected with reference to the text of the international application as filed (EP.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the translation for entry into the national phase (PCT Article 22 vs 39)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PCT Article 22: description, claims (if amended, both as originally filed and as amended, if applicant wishes amendments to form the basis for proceedings, together with any statement under PCT Article 19(1)), any text matter of drawings, abstract. Under PCT Article 39(1): description, claims, any text matter of drawings (if any of those parts has been amended, both as originally filed and as amended by the annexes to the IPRP Chapter II and claims amended under PCT Article 19, if applicant wishes these amendments to form the basis), abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only one translation (of original or amended parts) is furnished the Office will invite the applicant to furnish the missing translation within a reasonable time; failure may lead to deemed withdrawal. If translation of claims amended under PCT Article 19 is not furnished in due time, only those claims will be disregarded (PCT Rule 49.5(c‑bis)) and the international application will not be considered withdrawn (see footnote 1). Additional specific elements (e.g. Rule 13bis deposit references, sequence listings, statements under Article 19(1) and letters under PCT Rule 46.5(b)) must be furnished in an EPO official language when applicable (EP.03). When EPO acts as elected Office additional annexes to the IPRP (Chapter II) must be translated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is a copy of the international application required?
rubrics_metrics.description: No.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a copy is nonetheless relevant or helpful, follow EPO guidance, but the Official position in the summary is that a copy is not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees — currency, filing fee and page fee general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: National fees are payable in Euro (EUR). Within the 31‑month limit the European filing fee (composed of a basic fee and a page fee for the 36th and each subsequent page) must be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic filing fee is reduced where EPO Form 1200 is filed via EPO Online Filing, Online Filing 2.0 or the EPO Web‑Form Filing service. If the basic filing fee and/or page fee is not paid in full in due time, the application will be deemed withdrawn. The Euro‑PCT application will not be considered part of the state of the art under EPC Article 54(3) if fees are not paid (EP.05a). Page fee is based on international publication as a general rule and special counting rules apply if publication language and amendments are mixed (EP.05b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of payment and deposit account rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Payments via a deposit account held with the EPO are only accepted if made online, i.e. in an electronically processable format (XML) using EPO electronic filing forms, Online Fee Payment or Central Fee Payment service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refund instructions to a deposit account must also be filed in an electronically processable format. See Annex EP.I and Arrangements for deposit accounts (ADA) for details (EP.05).

rubrics_metrics.name: Page fee calculation rules and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Page fee is based on the international application as published: pages of the description, claims and drawings counted, plus one page in total for bibliographic data and abstract. Amended claims under PCT Article 19 and/or Article 34 are also considered part of the international publication and must be taken into account unless applicant indicates otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If parts of description/claims are amended on entry, the amended pages replace equivalent pages of the published international application and form the basis for calculating the page fee. Special rules apply if the international application was not published in an official EPO language and amendments are filed on entry. Pages amended after expiry of the 31‑month time limit are not counted. Page fees are not refunded if number of pages is reduced during proceedings (EP.05b). Completion of section 6 of Form 1200 helps to indicate which documents will form the basis for proceedings and compute the page fee correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: European designation fee (timing and consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: A flat designation fee must be paid within six months from the publication by the International Bureau of the international search report or before the expiry of the time limit applicable under PCT Articles 22(3) and 39(1)(b) and EPC Rule 159(1) (31 months), whichever expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the designation fee is not paid in due time the Euro‑PCT application will be deemed withdrawn (EP.06).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension/validation to extension/validation States
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications entering the European phase can be extended to or validated in certain States with Extension/Validation Agreements with the European Patent Organisation provided the Agreement was in force at the international filing date, the State was designated in the international application and the extension/validation fees have been paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension/validation fees are payable within the same deadlines as designation fees. If designation fee paid but extension/validation fees not paid, no communication is issued but the applicant may still pay fees with a 50% surcharge within a two‑month grace period after the basic time limit. When an extension State accedes to the EPC the Extension Agreement remains applicable to earlier international applications (EP.07).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims fees (when payable and calculation)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application documents on which the European grant procedure is to be based contain more than fifteen claims, a claims fee is payable within the 31‑month period in respect of the 16th and each subsequent claim; a higher claims fee applies for the 51st and each subsequent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims fees are calculated on the number of claims specified to form the basis for further proceedings on entry (including amended claims under PCT Articles 19 or 34(2) if these are to form the basis). If applicant fails to pay correct amount within 31 months, EPO will invite payment of the missing amount within the non‑extendable six‑month limit set in the communication under EPC Rules 161 and 162. If a claim fee is not paid in due time a noting of loss of rights (EPC Rule 112(1)) is issued and applicant may request further processing (EPC Article 121) by paying missing claims fees together with the fee for further processing within two months of notification; features of a claim deemed abandoned cannot subsequently be reintroduced (EP.08).

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of the inventor (when required)
rubrics_metrics.description: A designation of inventor must be filed upon entry into the European phase only if within the 31‑month limit the inventor has not been designated or certain information (e.g. country/place of residence) is missing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not filed upon entry the EPO will invite the applicant to file missing information within two months from notification of a communication under Rule 163(1) or (4) EPC; failure to furnish the missing information within that two‑month limit leads to refusal (EP.09). Legalisation is not required; see Annex EP.III for the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who can act as agent / Representation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Any professional representative entered on the list maintained by the EPO, or any legal practitioner qualified to practise in patent matters in one of the States party to the EPC and having place of business in that State, may act as agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural or legal persons having residence or principal place of business within an EPC contracting state may act on their own behalf. Natural or legal persons not having either must be represented by a professional representative and act through him in all EPC proceedings (EP.10). If required professional representative not appointed the EPO will invite appointment within two months; failure to correct leads to refusal. Payments can be made by anybody. Power of attorney generally need not be filed by a professional representative on the EPO list but they must inform the EPO of appointment; legal practitioners or employees representing an applicant under EPC Article 133(3) must always file a signed authorization or reference to a general authorization already on file. If authorization is required and not filed within the specified period, procedural steps taken by the agent will be deemed not to have been taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power(s) of attorney and general authorisations (form and registration)
rubrics_metrics.description: A power of attorney ('Authorisation' or 'General Authorisation') need not generally be filed by a professional representative on the EPO list but must be filed by legal practitioners or employees who are not professional representatives. General authorisations and sub‑authorisations have specific registration and content requirements (names, addresses, place of business, who may sign etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms EPO 1003 and 1004 and related Annexes give samples; where there are several authorisors special instructions apply and termination/registration rules apply. An authorisation signed by a person not entitled to sign will be treated as unsigned. See Annex EP.IV and EP.V and EP text for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal fees — timing and late payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Renewal fees are payable for the third and each subsequent year following the international filing date and must be paid before the expiration of the month containing the anniversary of the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment can still be made with a 50% surcharge before expiry of the sixth month after that month. A renewal fee due within the 31‑month time limit can be paid without surcharge up to the expiration of the 31‑month limit; it can still be paid within six months after 31 months subject to 50% surcharge. Failure to pay within the six‑month period means the application is deemed withdrawn; remedy possible by re‑establishment of rights under EPC Article 122 and Rule 136. Third year fee may not be paid validly more than six months before due; other renewal fees not more than three months before due (EP.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for examination (requirement to start substantive examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: A European patent will be granted only if substantive examination shows it meets EPC requirements; examination will only start upon explicit request (use EPO Form 1200 box 4.1). The request for examination is not deemed filed until the examination fee has been paid (EP.12).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must make the request and pay the examination fee within the applicable time limit (see EP.13 and EP.14); otherwise the Euro‑PCT application is deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for requesting examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination must be requested within six months from publication by the International Bureau of the international search report or before the expiration of the time limit under PCT Articles 22(3) and 39(1)(b) and EPC Rule 159(1) (31 months), whichever time limit expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the request or pay the examination fee in due time results in the Euro‑PCT application being deemed withdrawn (EP.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination fee — payment, reductions and refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for examination is effective only if the examination fee has been paid. The fee is reduced by 75% where an IPRP (Chapter II) has been established by the EPO; a further 30% reduction is available to SMEs, natural persons, non‑profits, universities or public research organisations of certain EPC contracting states when filing in an admissible non‑EPO language with a declaration (EP.14).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If both reductions apply, the 75% reduction is applied first and the 30% applied to the result (total reduction 82.5%). The examination fee is refunded in full if the application is withdrawn, refused or deemed withdrawn before substantive examination has begun. Fifty percent is refunded if withdrawn or refused after substantive examination has begun but before a certain procedural cut‑off (invitation under Article 94(3) or communication under Rule 71(3)) (EP.14). See Annex EP.I for amounts and reduction eligibility details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of non‑fulfilment of certain requirements (deemed withdrawal and further processing)
rubrics_metrics.description: EPC Rule 160: if translation of the international application or the request for examination is not filed in due time or if specified fees (filing, page, search, examination, designation) are not paid in due time, the European patent application is deemed withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant will be informed of deemed withdrawal and EPC Rule 112(2) applies. Loss of rights shall be deemed not to have occurred if, within two months of EPO notification, further processing is requested by payment of the respective fee(s) and the omitted act is completed. If both request for examination and payment of examination fee are missing, further processing must be requested in respect of both omissions and the applicant must file the request and pay the fee together with two fees for further processing (a flat fee and 50% of the examination fee) (EP.15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary European search — when performed and applicant options
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, a supplementary European search must be performed for each international application entering the European phase and a search fee must be paid. The search will be based on the last set of (amended) claims available to the EPO on the date of expiry of the time limit under EPC Rule 161(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request for examination was filed before transmittal of the supplementary search report, EPO invites applicant after transmittal to indicate whether to proceed further; applicant may waive the communication. Applicant may reply by filing amendments and/or comments. Applicant is required to reply to a negative written opinion within the time limit set in the communication under EPC Rule 70a(2). Where no supplementary search is performed because the ISR was established by the EPO, dispensation applies and no search fee is payable; the applicant is invited to comment on the ISA written opinion or the IPRP and may amend within six months (EP.16a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fee — payment, reductions and refunds
rubrics_metrics.description: If a supplementary European search report is to be established a search fee must be paid within the 31‑month limit. The search fee may be reduced (e.g. by EUR 1,185 where the ISR or a supplementary ISR was established by specified offices) and may be refunded fully or in part where the supplementary European search report is based on an earlier search report prepared by the Office (EP.16b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific list of Offices qualifying for reduction is set out (Austrian Patent Office, PRH, Nordic Patent Institute, Spanish PTO, PRV, Turkpatent, Visegrad Patent Institute) and reductions apply also when supplementary international search was established by those Offices. See EP text for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions, reductions or refunds of fees (general categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: No search fee is payable where the ISR has been established by the EPO. Search fees may be reduced for ISRs from specified Offices. Examination fee is reduced by 75% where IPRP Chapter II has been established by the EPO and further reduced by 30% for certain applicants filing in admissible non‑EPO languages (EP.14; EP.15 summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where conditions for reductions overlap the order of application and combined percentage reduction rules apply (see EP.14). Refunds of examination fees are available under specified circumstances; search fee refunds possible where supplementary European search is based on earlier Office search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Furnishing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Furnishing of a nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listing is required if it is not otherwise available to the EPO (see Special requirements of the Office (PCT Rule 51bis)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not already complied with within the 31‑month time limit the Office will invite the applicant to comply within two months; failure may lead to withdrawal. See OJ EPO and Guidelines references in text for format and particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name, address, nationality and residence information (applicant/inventor) obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Name, country and place of residence of the inventor and address, nationality and residence of the applicant must be furnished if not already included in the Request part of the international application or a PCT declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If missing the EPO will invite the applicant to furnish missing information within two months; failure to furnish may lead to refusal (EP.09 and EP text). Appointment of an agent is required if applicant has neither residence nor principal place of business in an EPC contracting state.
